evidence.claim: The older crossing used Indian Gap Road, completed in 1839 beside an old Cherokee trail.

evidence.claim: In 1872, Arnold Guyot's measurements established Newfound Gap as a lower pass, two miles east of Indian Gap.
evidence.quote: Newfound Gap was not recognized as the lowest gap over the mountains until 1872, when Arnold Guyot measured many of the mountains in the area and determined the "Newfound Gap" to be a lower, more accessible mountain pass.

evidence.claim: A wooden flume carries diverted Mingus Creek water to two turbines that power Mingus Mill.
evidence.quote: Water diverted from Mingus Creek via a sluice, and a wooden flume turns two turbines which provide power to the mill.

evidence.claim: An iron shaft connects them to grindstones downstairs and grain-cleaning equipment above.
evidence.quote: An iron shaft connects the turbines to grindstones on the first floor and a wheat cleaner and bolting chest on the second floor

evidence.claim: Tennessee millwright Sion Thomas Early built the mill for John Mingus in 1886, finishing in three months for $600.
evidence.quote: Mingus Mill was built in 1886 by the millwright Sion Thomas Early of Sevier County, Tennessee. Early did the work for John Mingus, a son of John Jacob Mingus. Early completed the mill in three months for a cost of $600.

evidence.claim: Aden Carver helped with that construction and returned in his nineties to assist the 1937 restoration.
evidence.quote: Aden Carver, who arrived in Oconaluftee in the mid-19th century, helped Early build the mill in 1886.  When the mill was restored in 1937, Carver, then in his 90s, aided in its restoration.

evidence.claim: After closing during World War II, the mill reopened in 1968.
evidence.quote: The mill was restored in 1937, closed during World War II, and reopened in 1968.

evidence.claim: Inside, a bucket belt lifts grain for cleaning before it drops back to the first-floor grindstones to become flour or cornmeal.
evidence.quote: Wheat or corn is first transported by bucket belt to the wheat cleaner, which is essentially a fan which clears the grain of dirt and excess material, and then drops it back to the first floor. The cleaned grain is then fed into the grindstones, which break it down into flour (or cornmeal).

evidence.claim: The Mountain Farm Museum beside the Oconaluftee Visitor Center gathers log buildings from different parts of the park.
evidence.quote: Adjacent to the Oconaluftee Visitor Center is the Mountain Farm Museum. The museum is a collection of several log buildings from various places around the park

evidence.claim: They were brought here in the 1950s to depict European-American farm life in Appalachia.
evidence.quote: In the 1950s, several log structures were moved to an area adjacent to the Oconaluftee Visitor Center to form the Mountain Farm Museum, which provides an exhibition of pioneer European-American life in Appalachia.

evidence.claim: The John Davis Cabin came from Indian Creek; its chestnut logs meet in dovetail notches.
evidence.quote: This cabin was originally located on Indian Creek several miles to the west neaar Bryson City. Davis moved to the area in 1885 to free-range his livestock. The cabin was constructed with chestnut logs joined with dove-tail notches.

evidence.claim: The Enloe Barn traveled only 200 yards from its original site in Oconaluftee.
evidence.quote: This is the only structure that was originally located in Oconaluftee, being moved only 200 yards (180 m) from its original location.

evidence.claim: Its roof has more than 16,000 hand-split shingles.
evidence.quote: The roof consists of over 16,000 hand-split shingles.
